title: First Draft: Why Is Israel Running TV Ads in Iowa Ahead of the Midterms?
author: Andrew Perez
content:
_On this day in 1973, President Richard Nixon oversaw the "Saturday Night
Massacre," in which Attorney General Elliot Richardson and Deputy AG William
Ruckelshaus resigned rather than fire Watergate Special Prosecutor Archibald
Cox. A moment long considered an extreme example of the abuse of presidential
power, it was eclipsed the moment Donald Trump showed up._

Good morning. **Andrew** here, as we recap another batshit day in Trump's
second-term America. One strange development: Israel - not the U.S. Israel
lobby, AIPAC, but the state of Israel - is running TV ads in a key
battleground state, with just two weeks left before the midterm elections.
Stranger still? You'll have to keep reading.

In today's **' First Draft,'** Israel wants Iowans to see video from one very
special president's special celebrations, plus **Donald Trump** and **JD
Vance** make their own extremely special contributions to the GOP's bizarre
midterms campaign. Let's read in.

The 2026 primary season was defined, in large part, by AIPAC's efforts to
meddle in Democratic primaries - and voters' rejection of the pro-Israel's
massive super PAC spending.

The midterm elections two weeks from today will likely be defined by the
illegal, reckless war into which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
[helped drag](https://zeteo.com/p/first-draft-trump-iran-marco-rubio-israel)
Donald Trump, America's very dumb president - and the costs that war with Iran
has imposed on virtually everyone in the U.S.: higher gas and fuel prices,
rising inflation, declining real wages.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Now, the state of Israel - not AIPAC, to be clear - is running television ads
in Iowa, a key Senate battleground state that may only be in play for
Democrats thanks to the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

In [one TV ad](https://x.com/emaroe1116/status/2111065621114867821), Israel
specifically touts its willingness to wage war. "**Israel confronts Iran and
its network of proxies directly, addressing those dangers at their source, "**
the ad says, claiming that this helps **" deter aggression"** and **" stop a
wider conflict"** - as if America isn't currently at war with Iran.

**" For Americans, the benefit is straightforward,"** the ad claims.

It's all highly unusual, though it has not attracted media attention. Upon
closer inspection, things get more unusual still.
